A sewing machine skips stitches when the needle fails to catch the bobbin thread on every cycle. On a second hand machine, the most common causes are simple setup issues, worn parts, or incorrect timing.

Start with the needle. Replace it with a new needle of the correct type and size for your fabric. A bent, blunt, or damaged needle is the most frequent cause of skipped stitches. Insert it fully and make sure the flat side faces the direction specified in the manual.

Remove both threads and thread the machine again with the presser foot raised. Raising the foot opens the tension discs so the upper thread can sit correctly between them. Check that the thread passes through every guide and through the needle in the correct direction. Then remove and reinsert the bobbin, confirming that it unwinds in the direction shown by the machine.

Use good quality thread and make sure the needle suits the material. Stretch fabric usually needs a stretch or ballpoint needle, while tightly woven fabric may require a sharp needle. A needle that is too small for thick thread can also miss stitches.

Clean lint from the bobbin area, feed dogs, and shuttle. Check the bobbin case for scratches, loose thread, or damage. Also confirm that the presser foot is attached securely and that you are not pulling the fabric while sewing.

If the machine still skips stitches with a new needle, correct threading, and ordinary cotton fabric, its needle bar height or hook timing may be wrong. This can happen after wear, impact, or previous repairs. Timing adjustments require precision, so a sewing machine technician should inspect it. A professional cleaning and service is often worthwhile for a recently purchased second hand machine, especially if its maintenance history is unknown.
quality_reasoning: The response fully explains why a sewing machine skips stitches, covering all the common causes (needle, threading, bobbin, timing) with practical, actionable guidance tailored to someone who has just bought a second hand machine.
